items.claim: The row's cross-seam catchword citation misidentifies the Hebrew bigram that actually recurs between the two mobilization calls, and its second Hebrew-to-English pairing quotes a shorter Hebrew span than the English rendering placed beside it.
items.evidence: The row cites בָּבֶ֜ל שְׂאוּ as 'the same two-word call' recurring from Jer.51.12 into Jer.51.27, but that exact pair does not occur at 51.27 at all; the bigram that actually recurs verbatim between the two verses is שְׂאוּ נֵ֗ס at 51.12 and שְׂאוּ נֵ֣ס at 51.27 (same two words, differing only in cantillation), which the row never cites. Separately, at 51.27 the row pairs the Hebrew directly with the English “Set up a standard in the land! Blow the trumpet among the nations!”, but the Hebrew quoted corresponds only to the clause rendered as the verse's first sentence, while the English continues into the following, unquoted sentence.

items.claim: The row's colophon citation and date-frame disclaimer both collate correctly, but one Hebrew-to-English pairing quotes a shorter Hebrew span than the English beside it, and one sentence names the writer's own production-tiling unit rather than a textual one.
items.evidence: At Jer.51.59 the row pairs the Hebrew הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֣ה יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֗יא directly with the English “The word which Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah”, but the Hebrew quoted stops before אֶת שְׂרָיָ֣ה, the object naming Seraiah, which only the English names. Separately, the sentence stating that the row 'and the part, end exactly at the byte-asserted colophon' names a production-tiling unit alongside the textual one; that unit has no literary-critical standing and does not belong among the boundary grounds. The colophon citation at 51.64 and the header-internal date at 51.59 are themselves accurate and correctly distinguished from the sleep-noun homograph used earlier in the chapter.
